This page covers what [Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/) does that a reader did not expect: a setting that changes nothing, a response with no cache status, a purge that leaves a copy behind, and the errors the API returns when it rejects a cache setting or a purge.

---

## A saved cache setting has no effect and responses stay `MISS`

Every response for the path reports `x-cache: MISS`, and the origin sees the same traffic as before the setting was saved.

A cache setting applies to no request until a [Rules Engine](/en/documentation/platform/applications/rules-engine/) rule names it. Creating the setting on the **Cache Settings** tab stores it; the **Set Cache Policy** behavior of a **Request Phase** rule is what puts it in effect. A rule saved in the last few minutes can also still be propagating.

- **Create the rule**: add a **Request Phase** rule whose criteria match the path and whose **Behaviors** carry **Set Cache Policy** with this setting. For the steps, refer to [Create a cache setting](/en/documentation/guides/application-performance/cache-and-purge/tune-cache-settings/).
- **Wait for propagation**: a new rule can take a few minutes to apply.
- **Check the status again**: request the object with the debug header and read `x-cache`. For the request, refer to [Check the cache status of a response](/en/documentation/guides/application-performance/cache-and-purge/check-page-cache-time/).

Once the rule applies the setting, the first request stores the copy and reports `MISS`, and a response answered from that copy reports `HIT`.

---

## `x-cache` reports `-` on every response for a path

The response carries `x-cache: -` and `x-cache-key: -`, with no status and no key.

A `-` means the content is restricted from caching. The documented case is the request method: Azion caches `GET` and `HEAD` natively, and a `POST` or `OPTIONS` request is not cached until the cache setting varies by that method, which requires [Application Accelerator](/en/documentation/build/application-accelerator/) on the application.

- **Turn on method caching**: in the cache setting, under **Application Accelerator**, open **Cache vary by Method** and select the method. For the steps, refer to [Cache POST and OPTIONS responses](/en/documentation/guides/application-performance/cache-and-purge/cache-post-and-options-responses/).
- **Confirm the module is on**: the field is rejected with error `21013` while Application Accelerator is off on the application.

A cached method then reports a status and a key, and the key ends with the MD5 hash of the request body. For the key format, refer to [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/).

---

## Content is still served from cache after a Bypass Cache rule

A **Bypass Cache** rule matches the path, and requests are still answered from a stored copy instead of the origin.

**Bypass Cache** affects Azion's cache and not the [Tiered Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/tiered-cache/) layer. An application whose cache settings have Tiered Cache on keeps caching objects in that layer for the minimum TTL of the setting, and the first layer can be answered from there.

- **Turn Tiered Cache off** on the cache setting that covers the path, in the **Cache** section of the setting. For the field, refer to [Cache settings](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-settings/).
- **Purge the Tiered Cache layer** by cache key, then purge Cache, so the first layer is not refilled from the second. For the steps, refer to [Purge cached content](/en/documentation/guides/application-performance/cache-and-purge/purge-cached-content/).

A request that reaches the origin through the rule reports `x-cache: BYPASS`.

---

## A purge did not expire a variation of the object

A purge was accepted, and requests still receive the previous content for some visitors or some arguments.

A URL purge converts each URL to one cache key and ignores content variation. A copy that varies by cookie, device group, or image format therefore survives it. Variation by query string is the exception, and even there the arguments have to be in the order the key holds them, or in alphabetical order when **Sort** is on in the cache setting.

- **Purge by cache key**, listing every variation of the object, up to 50 keys per request.
- **Purge by wildcard**, with `@@*` at the end for cookie, device, and method variations, or `?*` for query-string variations.
- **Read the keys first**: the `x-cache-key` header of a response shows the key that variation produced. For the format, refer to [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/).

Every variation then returns `x-cache: MISS` on its next request. For what each purge type reaches, refer to [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/).

---

## The API rejects a Max Age below 60 seconds with error `21021`

A `POST` or `PATCH` on a cache setting answers with HTTP `400` and the title `Edge Cache Max Age Lower Than The Minimum Allowed By Application's Application Accelerator Module`. The error names `meta.min_value` as `60`.

The cache TTL has a floor of 60 seconds, and [Application Accelerator](/en/documentation/build/application-accelerator/) lifts it to 0 seconds. The application in the request path does not have the module on.

- **Turn on the module**: in the application, under **Main Settings** > **Modules**, turn on **Application Accelerator** and select **Save**.
- **Or raise the value**: set **Max Age** to 60 seconds or more.

The setting then saves with the value you sent. For the floor and the ceiling, refer to [Cache limits](/en/documentation/build/cache/limits/).

---

## Tiered Cache cannot be turned on and the API returns `21001` or `21020`

A cache setting that carries `tiered_cache.enabled` as `true` is rejected with HTTP `400`, under one of two titles.

`It's Not Possible To Use This Edge Cache Behavior.` means the setting's cache behavior is `honor`; Tiered Cache requires _Override cache behavior_. `Edge Cache Max Age Lower Than The Minimum Allowed By The Tiered Cache Module` means **Max Age** is below 3 seconds, the floor the layer requires.

- **Set the behavior to override** and give **Max Age** at least 3 seconds, in the same request.
- **From the Azion CLI, send the body with `--file`**: the `--tiered-caching-enabled` flag alone always hits `21001`, because no flag sets the cache behavior.

The setting then saves, and reading it back shows `tiered_cache` with `enabled` set to `true`. For the conditions and the topologies, refer to [Tiered Cache](/en/documentation/build/cache/tiered-cache/).

---

## A cache setting cannot be deleted and the API returns `21014`

A `DELETE` on a cache setting answers with HTTP `400`, the title `Cannot Delete Cache Setting`, and the detail `This Cache Setting cannot be deleted because it is being used.`

A rule still names the setting in its **Set Cache Policy** behavior. A setting in use by a rule cannot be removed.

- **Find the rule** on the **Rules Engine** tab of the application, and either point its **Set Cache Policy** behavior at another setting or delete the rule.
- **Repeat the deletion** once no rule names the setting.

The `DELETE` then succeeds and the setting leaves the **Cache Settings** list.

---

## A purge request is rejected with `30001`, `30003`, or `30005`

A purge answers with HTTP `400` instead of `201`, under one of three titles.

- **`30001`, `Invalid Purge Layer For Purge Type`**: the request sends `layer` as `tiered_cache` on a URL or wildcard purge. Purge the Tiered Cache layer by cache key, or set the layer to `cache`.
- **`30003`, `Unauthorized Domain`**: an item names a domain the account does not own. A purge reaches only the domains of the account that sends it.
- **`30005`, `Invalid Purge Cachekey`**: an item of a cache key purge is not a valid cache key. Send the key exactly as the `x-cache-key` header returns it, with no scheme separator and no spaces. For the format, refer to [Cache keys](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-keys/).

An accepted purge answers with HTTP `201` and `state` set to `executed`. For the bodies and the layers, refer to [Real-Time Purge](/en/documentation/build/cache/real-time-purge/).

---

## The Azion CLI prints an empty error object

A `create` or `update` on a cache setting fails, and with `--format json` the output carries `{"error": {}}` instead of a reason.

Azion CLI 4.23.0 drops the API's message when the output format is JSON. The API did return a code and a title; the CLI did not print them.

- **Run the command again without `--format json`**: the plain output carries the API's message, such as `It's not possible to use this edge cache behavior while using Tiered Cache.`
- **Match the message** against the errors on this page or on [Cache settings](/en/documentation/build/cache/cache-settings/), which lists every code the endpoint returns.

The plain output names the field and the reason, which is enough to correct the request.
